name: Block / Parry System
description: The defensive verb pair: block reduces a confirmed hit to chip, parry voids it entirely inside a tight window. They live in one component because they share the same upstream fact — combat.hit_confirmed — and differ only in timing and cost; two components would race each other to answer the same event. This component owns the guard state, the parry window, and the guard-integrity meter that makes turtling expensive, and it deliberately stops there: the damage that chip reduces, and the stun a parry inflicts, are computed by combat.damage_resolver and combat.status_effects respectively, because the moment a block system starts applying its own damage math there are two resolvers and every balance pass touches both. Punish logic after a parry is likewise not here — a parry emits its fact, and combat.combo_chain decides what the defender is now allowed to do with the advantage.

inputs.name: parryWindowFrames
inputs.description: Frames after the parry input during which a confirmed hit is voided. Four is deliberately ungenerous — parry is the high-risk answer; block is the safe one.

inputs.name: blockstunFrames
inputs.description: Base frames the defender is locked after blocking. Per-move overrides come from the attacker's frame data; this is the fallback.

inputs.name: chipDamageFraction
inputs.description: Fraction of a hit's damage that leaks through block, passed to combat.damage_resolver rather than applied here. Zero makes block free and rounds stall; 0.1 keeps pressure honest.

inputs.name: guardIntegrityMax
inputs.description: The meter that drains per blocked hit and breaks at zero. Guard break converts infinite blocking into a resource decision.

inputs.name: guardRegenPerSecond
inputs.description: Integrity recovered per second while not blocking. Regen only when disengaged, so resetting to neutral is the way to heal your guard.
